title: Isolating Nuclei from Human Stem Cell-Derived Grafts for snRNA Sequencing
author: Sozzi, Storm, et al.

steps.title: Prepare dissection workstation
steps.instruction: Wipe all work surfaces and the dissection microscope with 70 % ethanol and RNaseZAP, turn on the microscope and adjust illumination, arrange a sterile glass or plastic Petri dish, spring scissors, straight forceps, and a fine‑tipped paintbrush next to the microscope, set up a box of dry ice and pre‑label one 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube per graft slice, and wear gloves and a face mask throughout.

steps.title: Dissect graft from brain slices
steps.instruction: Transfer the brain slices (from the vibratome step) together with chilled, carbogen‑saturated aCSF into the Petri dish, keep slices fully submerged, identify the graft (typically present in 2–4 consecutive slices; use GFP fluorescence if available or anatomical landmarks), cut around the graft with spring scissors without disturbing surrounding tissue, pick up each dissected graft with a paintbrush or straight forceps and place it into a pre‑labeled 1.5 mL tube, snap‑freeze the tubes on dry ice and then store them at –80 °C (up to 2 years, avoiding freeze‑thaw cycles).

steps.title: Set up nuclei extraction station
steps.instruction: Clean the bench, pipettes and tube racks with RNaseZAP, place glass douncers on regular ice, pre‑cool the centrifuge to 4 °C and ensure adapters are chilled, label two DNA LoBind 1.5 mL tubes per sample (plus one extra for FANS re‑analysis), prepare on ice a lysis buffer (1 mL per sample) and a resuspension buffer (600 µL per sample) and supplement the lysis solution with DTT, Triton X‑100 and RNase inhibitors; for eight mature grafts, 10 mL lysis buffer and 5 mL resuspension buffer are typically sufficient.

steps.title: Lyse and homogenize frozen graft tissue
steps.instruction: Thaw the dissected grafts on ice for 5 min, add 500 µL cold lysis buffer directly to each tube and gently pipette up and down with a P1000 to detach tissue, transfer the tissue and any remaining buffer into a pre‑chilled glass douncer, add an additional 500 µL cold lysis buffer, homogenize with a loose‑fitting pestle for 10–15 strokes then with a tight‑fitting pestle for another 10–15 strokes until the solution is uniformly cloudy with small bubbles, transfer the lysate to a cold LoBind tube and centrifuge at 900 g for 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Coat collection tubes and prepare DRAQ7 buffer
steps.instruction: On ice add 100 µL resuspension buffer to the designated re‑analysis tube, add DRAQ7 to the remaining resuspension buffer at a 1:1000 dilution and mix gently, coat each DNA LoBind collection tube by adding up to 200 µL of the DRAQ7‑containing buffer, keep all tubes on ice (coating must be performed at least 30 min before sorting).

steps.title: Resuspend nuclear pellet
steps.instruction: After centrifugation, carefully aspirate and discard the supernatant with a P200 pipette without disturbing the pellet, flick the tube bottom to detach the pellet, add 200–400 µL of the DRAQ7‑supplemented resuspension buffer (volume adjusted to graft size) and keep on ice; optionally filter the suspension through a 40 µm nylon mesh for cell pellets or organoids (not recommended for graft samples).

steps.title: Purify nuclei by FANS
steps.instruction: Set up the cell sorter with a 100 µm nozzle and activate the 640 nm red laser for DRAQ7 detection, establish gating: exclude debris (P1), select DRAQ7‑positive nuclei (P2), remove doublets using SSC‑W vs SSC‑A (P3) and FSC‑H vs FSC‑A (P4); run an unstained control the first time, sort approximately 200–500 nuclei into the re‑analysis tube, re‑analyze to confirm purity, then sort each sample into its pre‑coated collection tube, keep all tubes on ice after sorting.

steps.title: Generate 10× snRNA‑seq libraries
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the nuclei suspension at 500 g for 10 min at 4 °C, carefully remove the supernatant and retain a final volume of 34 µL for loading, thaw all 10× Genomics reagents on ice, load the nuclei suspension and reagents into a Chromium Chip according to the manufacturer’s instructions, perform GEM generation and library preparation using the 10× Single Cell 3′ (v3.1 or later) protocol adapted for nuclei, and verify library size and integrity by loading 1 µL on an Agilent Bioanalyzer.
